name: Vanthorpe Meridian Wristband Comm MK-1
description: Slim brushed-titanium cuff, 22mm wide, with a recessed micro-display across the outer face that reads clean biometric data, message queues, and calendar blocks in cool white text. The inner band is soft medical-grade polymer, shaped to seat flush against augmented or unaugmented wrists alike. Available in satin titanium or matte carbon. Understated enough for a board meeting, readable enough for a factory floor supervisor who got promoted.
functionality: Biometric monitoring, encrypted message relay, calendar and transit sync, NFC payment chip, 72-hour battery life. BCI-readable with standard neural port handshake. Haptic alert pulse.
what_it_says: Competent, connected, and careful about how much they show — this person lives and dies by their schedule.
story_hooks: The MK-1 firmware has a known exploit that lets a nearby device silently mirror its message queue — Vanthorpe issued a patch, but millions of units were never updated.
A dead Tier 3 auditor is found with her MK-1 wiped clean — but the wipe timestamp is three hours after her estimated time of death.
Someone is paying Φ2,000 cash for specific MK-1 serial number ranges, no questions asked.
